PRENATAL CYTOGENETICS LABORATORY REPORT
[redacted location] Regional Genetics Laboratory

PATIENT INFORMATION
Patient Name: [redacted name]
Date of Birth: [redacted date]
Medical Record Number: [redacted ID]
Referring Physician: Dr. [redacted name]
Date of Collection: [redacted date]
Date of Report: [redacted date]

CLINICAL INFORMATION
Indication for Testing: Prenatal testing at 16 weeks gestation per ultrasound
Sample Type: Amniotic fluid (uncultured)
Gestational Age: 16 weeks

TEST PERFORMED
Quantitative Fluorescence Polymerase Chain Reaction (QF-PCR) for rapid aneuploidy detection

METHODOLOGY
QF-PCR analysis was performed on uncultured amniotic fluid cells using fluorescently labeled primers for short tandem repeat (STR) markers on chromosomes 13, 18, and 21. A minimum of four informative markers were analyzed for each chromosome. The test detects the most common aneuploidies including trisomy 13 (Patau syndrome), trisomy 18 (Edwards syndrome), and trisomy 21 (Down syndrome). DNA was extracted using QIAamp DNA Mini Kit. PCR amplification was performed using the Devyser Compact v3 kit, and fragment analysis was carried out on an Applied Biosystems 3500 Genetic Analyzer.

RESULTS

Chromosome 13: Normal diallelic pattern observed
Informative markers: D13S631, D13S258, D13S742, D13S628
Conclusion: Two copies of chromosome 13 detected

Chromosome 18: Normal diallelic pattern observed
Informative markers: D18S391, D18S390, D18S535, D18S386
Conclusion: Two copies of chromosome 18 detected

Chromosome 21: Normal diallelic pattern observed
Informative markers: D21S1435, D21S1411, D21S1412, D21S1446
Conclusion: Two copies of chromosome 21 detected

MATERNAL CELL CONTAMINATION
Analysis of maternal cell contamination using polymorphic markers showed no evidence of significant maternal cell contamination in the fetal sample.

INTERPRETATION
QF-PCR analysis demonstrates a normal complement for chromosomes 13, 18, and 21. No aneuploidy detected for the tested chromosomes.

LIMITATIONS
1. This test is designed to detect whole chromosome aneuploidies of chromosomes 13, 18, and 21 only. Other chromosomal abnormalities, including structural rearrangements, microdeletions/duplications, and aneuploidies of other chromosomes, will not be detected.
2. Low-level mosaicism (<20%) may not be reliably detected by this method.
3. Triploidy may be suspected but cannot be definitively diagnosed by QF-PCR alone.
4. This test does not detect open neural tube defects or other congenital anomalies.
5. Maternal cell contamination, if present at high levels, could mask fetal aneuploidy.

RECOMMENDATIONS
Based on the normal QF-PCR results, no further chromosome analysis is needed on this sample for the indication provided. If ultrasound abnormalities are detected later in pregnancy or if there are other clinical concerns, additional testing such as chromosomal microarray or karyotype analysis may be considered.

This test was developed and validated by [redacted location] Regional Genetics Laboratory. Results should be interpreted in conjunction with clinical findings and other laboratory data.

Reported by: [redacted name], PhD, FACMG
Laboratory Director: [redacted name], MD, PhD
